sections.hyperkeratosis_causes_symptoms_treatment:
Abstract 

Skin is the largest organ of the body, and its disorders are rising day by day due to the toxic environmental conditions, sedentary lifestyle habits, stress, and altered climatic conditions. Many people struggle with issues such as acne, pimples, psoriasis, dermatitis, fungal infection, and eczema. Amongst all these conditions, one such condition is hyperkeratosis, which is the thickening of the outermost layer of the skin, which is the epidermis, which further results in hard, rough, and variable skin texture. In this article, we will discuss Hyperkeratosis in detail.
sections.introduction: Hyperkeratosis is a skin condition that is recognized by thickening of the outermost layer of the skin, called as stratum corneum. Hyperkeratosis is caused by excessive keratin accumulation on the outer surface of the skin. Keratin protects the skin, but when it is produced in larger amounts, it results in rough, damaged, hard, and pigmented patchy skin. It can occur at various body parts such as knees, elbows, scalp, face, hands, and feet. It can also occur from skin-related issues or from disturbances in various body systems. Long-term hyperkeratosis can lead to pain, discomfort, and cosmetic disfigurement.

 Pathogenesis 

Hyperkeratosis is a condition that is due to increased keratin production and thickening of the outermost layer of the skin. Factors that cause hyperkeratosis, such as irritation, inflammation, chemical exposure, genetic changes, or radiation exposure, result in multiplication of skin cells and prevent the shielding of the skin, which leads to dry, rough skin. Hyperkeratosis may occur in patches or in a continuous pattern, which mainly depends on the area affected.

sections.ayurvedic_overview_of_hyperkeratosis:
In ayurveda hyperkeratosis is described under twak vikara (skin disorders). It mainly occurs due to sedentary lifestyle and improper dietary habits. Mainly vata dosha is involved in this. When vata dosha gets aggravated it disturbs the equilibrium of kapha dosha which enters the minute bodily channels and causes obstruction. Due to obstruction, nourishment of dhatus got affected which causes abnormal overgrowth of mamsa (muscle) and meda dhatu (fat tissues). At the same time there is vitiation in dhatu balance; it leads to dry, rough, thick, discolouration of skin and may cause itching over the skin.


Ayurveda mainly emphasizes on balancing the doshas, dhatu, clearing the minute body channels and removing the thickened skin through some external ayurveda therapies. Treatment focuses on involving the use of classical formulations such as arogyavardhini vati, panchtikitghrit guggul, Punarnava mandoor and many more. Along with this detoxification therapies can be advised such as Udvartana (herbal powder massage) and raktmokshan (blood letting therapy) which helps in clearing the skin and improving its texture.
